project: CAPACITY CONNECT - AI-Powered Digital Capacity Building & Learning Management Platform
organization: India Meteorological Department (IMD), Ministry of Earth Sciences (MoES)
tagline: Learn. Build Skills. Connect Expertise. Measure Impact.
design_archetype: ARCHETYPE 1: ORGANIC & EARTHY / HIGH-CONTRAST ENTERPRISE TECH
theme_strategy: Light mode default with crisp deep navy structural accents, high contrast data density, subtle slate borders, and vibrant status indicators for competency mapping and radar analytics.

priority_demo_flow_steps: Step 1: Trainee Competency (AI Skill Gap Analyzer with Radar & Bar Charts)
Step 2: Personalized Learning Path (Interactive step-by-step interactive roadmap)
Step 3: Recommended Course (Detailed syllabus, competency tags, estimated effort)
Step 4: Enroll Action (Instant state updates with Sonner toast feedback)
Step 5: Course Material & Interactive Player (Video/Document module with chapter tracking)
Step 6: Assessment Flow (Smart Assessment engine with timer, mark for review, question palette, auto-save)
Step 7: Result & Competency Growth Feedback (Breakdown by Doppler Radar, Numerical Weather Modeling, Satellite Meteorology)
Step 8: Recommended Next Activity & Trainer Match (AI Trainer Matching algorithm with score & direct message/booking)
Step 9: Switch to Trainer Dashboard (Overview of trainees, course analytics, early warning for at-risk learners)
Step 10: AI Assessment Generator (Generate weather modeling question paper, review, edit, mandatory trainer review before publishing)
Step 11: Switch to Admin Dashboard (Organizational Competency Heatmap across IMD regions: HQ New Delhi, Regional Met Centers, NWP Center)
Step 12: Cybersecurity & Infrastructure Gap Analysis (Identify critical deficit in High-Performance Computing & Radar Cyber-defense, match trainers & courses)
Step 13: Training Impact Dashboard (Platform-measured skill delta analytics, explicitly labeled as internal learning data)

instructions_to_main_agent: Ensure the upper navbar displays official IMD / MoES branding elements: Ministry of Earth Sciences, Govt of India logo lockup styling, and official emblem tone.

Implement a prominent Demo Switcher banner at the top allowing seamless 1-click role switching between Trainee (Dr. Ananya Sharma), Trainer (Dr. Rajesh Kumar - Senior Radar Specialist), and Admin (Shri Vikramaditya - Director General Capacity Building).
Provide a quick 'Run Priority Demo Flow' guided wizard bar so reviewers can step through the entire 13-step flow automatically or manually.

Ensure every single interactive element, menu item, card action, button, input, tab, and metric carries a descriptive 'data-testid' attribute (e.g. data-testid='trainee-enroll-btn', data-testid='competency-heatmap-matrix').
Use Recharts for rendering radar charts (competencies), bar charts (learning progress & impact), and heatmap grid representations.
Do NOT use raw HTML select or date inputs; stick to custom dropdowns and Shadcn primitives styled with indigo/navy accents.

All AI features (Skill Gap Analyzer, Assessment Generator, CAPACITY AI Assistant) must respond instantly with realistic, domain-rich meteorological and earth science content without requiring external API keys.
UNIVERSAL GUIDELINES FOR MAIN AGENT: Dark colors look good when used independently without gradients. DO NOT use dark colors as gradients everywhere except dedicated AI feature containers.
Don't make generic centered layouts. Use asymmetrical grid layouts with wide breathing room (p-6, p-8).
Create depth through layered design elements with z-index hierarchy.
Use glass-morphism effects with backdrop filters (12-24px blur) for sticky navigation and action overlays.
You MUST NOT apply universal transition (transition: all). Always specify explicit properties (e.g., transition-colors duration-200).
You MUST NOT center align the app container (.App { text-align: center; }).
NEVER use raw emoji characters like 🤖🧠💭💡 for UI icons. Use Lucide or Phosphor icons exclusively.
Every interaction needs micro-animations: hover states, smooth state transitions, and toast feedback via Sonner.
